sm: P. Andrew Sandlin reflects on Romans chapter 1, where Paul lists the sins of the Gentile nations, and points out that ingratitude sits in the middle of that catalog. He says Paul treats the failure to give thanks as a sign of apostasy, rooted in the heart rather than in poor manners. Unbelievers credit their successes to their own strength and their troubles to bad luck, so God never enters their calculation. Sandlin cites Cornelius Van Til on man wanting to avoid thinking about God, and Bob Jones Sr. on the hopelessness of ungrateful people. He recalls his father teaching that a man who still has gratitude, however far he has fallen, still has hope. He rejects the idea of the self-made man and says everything good in life is a gift from God, so we are God-made. He closes by urging listeners not to be ingrates and to live in gratitude to God and to those who helped them.
